_description: Task13 WEIGHTING field, FINE transcription -- the 0.1mm grid used for BOTH the near-field solve and the final stitched volume, for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch. The coarse sibling (example_gen_pixel_with_grid_task13_coarse.json) is the 0.55mm far-field grid. THIS FILE AND example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_fine.json DEFINE THE SAME PAD SURFACE and must agree: pad top 10.00mm on both. PHASE 4 RETARGET: only the DEPTH moved in this file. Every geometry value is unchanged, because at 0.1mm every true design length is already an exact whole number of cells -- pixelSize 3.5 -> 35 cells, pixelGap 0.9 -> 9, chamfer_r 0.7 -> 7 (via int(round()) in the generator; 0.7/0.1 is 6.999999999999999 in binary float, so the rounding is load-bearing). NOTHING IS SNAPPED HERE, which is the opposite of the coarse file. NO CathodePotential AND NO GridPotential, AND DO NOT ADD THEM. The weighting potential is a DIMENSIONLESS UNIT PROBE in [0,1]: the collecting pixel is held at 1 and every other electrode, the cathode included, at 0. The drift pair's cathode formula does not apply, and the drift pair's 50.0 V/mm design field has no counterpart here. driftZDepth 149.55 is carried only so the file handed to induce-pixel is not stale; the weighting solve does not use a drift length. 1.1mm IS THE SHARED PERIOD of the 0.1mm and 0.55mm grids, and every plane that must land on both is a whole multiple of it: pitch 4.4 = 44 fine / 8 coarse cells, pad plane 9.9 = 99 / 18, interface 29.7 = 297 / 54, cathode 149.6 = 1496 / 272. The fine z grid is 1497 nodes and the near grid 298. PITCH: 3.5 + 0.9 = 4.4mm = 44 fine cells and 8 coarse cells of 0.55mm. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise. TRANSVERSE EXTENT: Npixels 5 at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm = 220 fine cells (40 coarse). The weighting probe is solved NON-PERIODIC over the whole tile -- edges fix,fix,fix -- so Npixels DOES size this file's domain, unlike the drift field's single periodic tile. PIXEL PLANE LOW EDGE 9.9 IS LOAD-BEARING: 9.9mm is 99 fine cells AND 18 coarse cells of 0.55mm, so the pad plane lands on a real node of BOTH grids. Moving it breaks that co-location. THE PAD SURFACE THIS FILE DEFINES IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. padThickness 0.05 and FR4Thickness 0.1 each round to ONE cell here (n_pad is clamped to a 1-cell minimum because 0.05 is half a cell), so the generator derives pp_width = n_pad + n_fr4 - 1 = 1 and the pad TOP is at (99+1)*0.1 = 10.00mm -- identical to the drift fine config. Both fields' near solves and ALL drift paths live on this grid, which is why the FINE pair is what must agree. The coarse grid's own pad top is 10.45mm; that 0.45mm disagreement is expected and is NOT to be compensated for. KNOWN OPEN DEFECT OF THE WEIGHTING SOLVE, measured not inferred (pochoir-h92v): the fix,fix,fix transverse edges are implemented as a NEUMANN MIRROR, not a Dirichlet zero (fdm_generic.py:8-34 -- the 'fixed' branch copies from the interior), so the 5x5 patch behaves as an INFINITE PERIODIC PAD ARRAY. W was measured falling essentially LINEARLY to zero from z ~ 30mm to the cathode -- the parallel-plate signature -- instead of decaying as an isolated pad's weighting potential would. The far tail is therefore unphysical. NOT fixed here. NO MEASURED NUMBERS SURVIVE FROM THE 8cm TRANSCRIPTION. Every such figure has been DELETED rather than carried over: different depth, different spacing, different interface. Do not reinstate any of it, and do not write a new number here until it has been measured -- Phase 4/Step 7 is where the far-W numbers for this geometry come from. pixelPlaneWidth 0.1 is INERT in this configuration: with enableInsulatorFR4 true and both thickness keys present, the generator derives pp_width and overwrites whatever this key says. SHIELD GRID OFF (GridHoleShape 'None'): inherited from the older with-grid task13 work, never intended for this WOGRID LArPix v2a geometry. PcbWidth and HoleRadius are inert and left in place.
